rounds.text: Active Clothing Co Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, trading at a steep discount with a DCF-derived intrinsic value leaving a massive 63.4% margin of safety at the current price of Rs 96 [E43, E44]. The current share price implies a modest 4.1% earnings growth against a base-case assumption of 18.0%, suggesting the market has completely overlooked the company's powerful fundamental trajectory [E45]. This disconnect is starkly highlighted by a 5-year compounded profit growth of 178% eclipsing the 32% compounded share price growth over the same period, confirming that fundamentals are dramatically outpacing market sentiment [E22, E46, E49]. Furthermore, the company trades at an attractive P/E of 14.37x compared to the sector benchmark of 15.88x while simultaneously outperforming sector efficiency metrics with an ROE of 10.82% versus 6.46% and an ROCE of 9.69% versus 8% [E6, E9, E10]. Operational quality is further reinforced by robust cash conversion of 1.40x in March 2026, alongside a 37.5% increase in capital work-in-progress pointing toward active growth investments [E33, E39]. Conceded: debt exceeds net worth with a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.40x alongside zero dividend yield and a negative free cash flow of Rs -3 Cr [E4, E35, E37, E50].

Active Clothing Co Ltd carries significant financial and operational vulnerabilities that weigh against its headline valuation. The company’s leverage is high, with a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.40x in March 2026, meaning debt exceeds net worth and borrowings have climbed to Rs 130 Cr [E37, E38]. This aggressive borrowing fails to generate immediate free cash, resulting in a negative free cash flow of Rs -3 Cr for March 2026 [E35]. Furthermore, historical return profiles remain lackluster, evidenced by a low median return on equity of just 6% over 10 years and 7% over 5 years [E25, E26]. Top-line expansion has also hit a near-term wall, with compounded sales growth decelerating to a meager 2% over the trailing twelve months [E17]. Compounded share price growth over the past year sits deeply in the negative at -15%, matching a complete zero percent dividend yield that leaves shareholders unrewarded for holding this risk [E4, E24]. conceded: [E43]

While the bear points to a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.40x and borrowings of Rs 130 Cr [E37, E38], this leverage is actively funding expansion, evidenced by Capital Work in Progress (CWIP) increasing by 37.5% to Rs 11 Cr [E39]. The negative free cash flow of Rs -3 Cr [E35] is a natural byproduct of this active capex build-up phase rather than structural failure, especially since operating cash flow remains robust at Rs 14 Cr with a healthy 1.40x cash conversion rate [E33, E34]. Regarding historical returns [E25, E26], the company's more recent profitability metrics show a decisive structural upturn, with a 3-year median ROE of 10% [E27], a TTM median ROE of 12% [E28], and a current ROE of 10.82% that outpaces the sector benchmark of 6.46% [E9]. While TTM sales growth has moderated to 2% [E17], this overlooks exceptional medium-term compounding, including a 34% 5-year and 16% 3-year sales growth rate [E15, E16], alongside stellar 5-year and 3-year profit growth of 178% and 64% respectively [E19, E20]. Finally, conceded: [E4] and conceded: [E24], yet the fundamental disconnect where 178% 5-year profit growth vastly outpaces a 32% share price growth [E22] indicates a market mispricing rather than operational decline, further supported by results scoring 81/100 with accelerating earnings [E57].

Conceded: [E39], but framing rising leverage and negative free cash flow as a mere growth phase glosses over the concrete risk that borrowings sit at Rs 130 Cr against a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.40x, leaving the company heavily indebted [E37, E38]. While the bull highlights operating cash flow of Rs 14 Cr and a 1.40x cash conversion rate [E33, E34], this fails to offset the reality of negative free cash flow standing at Rs -3 Cr [E35], which directly threatens liquidity. The reliance on recent ROE figures of 10% to 12% [E27, E28] ignores the company's weak long-term track record, highlighted by a 10-year median ROE of just 6% and a 5-year median ROE of 7% [E25, E26], as well as a low 3-year average ROE of 10.4% [E51]. Conceded: [E15, E16, E19, E20], yet citing historical compounding misses the severe deceleration occurring right now, where TTM sales growth has slammed down to a meager 2% [E17]. Finally, the stagnant share price performance yielding -15% over the past year [E24] combined with a complete lack of dividends at 0.00% [E4] demonstrates that shareholders are seeing zero cash return while bearing heavy balance-sheet risk [E37].
